label: Robert Garcia
narrative: Garcia was Ranking Member of the National Security, the Border and Foreign Affairs subcommittee when it held the 26 July 2023 hearing, and his handling of it is why the hearing read as an oversight proceeding rather than a spectacle. He opened by thanking Burchett for the leadership that produced the hearing, framed the matter as national security and institutional trust, and anchored it to the December 2017 New York Times reporting on DIA-funded UAP research. His questioning concentrated on the reporting gap: Graves's estimate of the number of pilots he was working with, the absence of any usable reporting channel for aviators, and the stigma that suppresses reports. He converted that into legislation - on 11 January 2024 he introduced H.R. 6967, the Safe Airspace for Americans Act, to let civilian pilots and personnel report UAP encounters to the FAA for onward transmission to AARO with legal safeguards, co-led with Republican subcommittee chairman Glenn Grothman. He attended the 12 January 2024 closed ICIG briefing and said afterward that everyone in the room 'probably received new information.' He is now Ranking Member of the full Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 119th Congress, which places the ranking-member half of the committee's UAP posture with him.
